# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Singh_2015_phi1_mouse_qsp"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12>

Singh and colleagues (*CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology*, 2015)
built the first parsimonious systems-pharmacology model of erythropoiesis in
mice, driven by an orally administered small-molecule inhibitor of
prolyl-hydroxylase-2 (PHD2) that the paper calls **PHI-1** (an undisclosed
Pfizer compound). Inhibiting PHD2 stabilises hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha
(HIF1alpha), which drives the cascade

> PHI-1 -> PHD2 inhibition -> kidney HIF1alpha -> kidney EPO mRNA ->
> plasma EPO -> reticulocytes -> red blood cells -> hemoglobin.

Male BALB/c mice received single oral doses of 10 or 30 mg/kg, and the
time courses of plasma PHI-1, kidney HIF1alpha, kidney EPO mRNA, plasma EPO,
reticulocytes, red blood cells (RBC) and hemoglobin (HGB) were measured. The
authors fitted the PK and the HIF1alpha / EPO-mRNA / plasma-EPO / reticulocyte
responses sequentially by naive-pooled maximum likelihood in ADAPT 5, and used
the model to *simulate* RBC, HGB and the (unmeasured) PHD2 activity ratio.

This is a **deterministic, typical-value mechanism model**: a naive-pooled fit
with no between-subject variability and no reported residual-error SDs, so the
model file carries no `eta` terms and no error model. The validation below
reproduces the published figures and checks baseline steady state and the
endogenous-EPO half-life, rather than using a stochastic VPC.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Singh_2015_phi1_mouse_qsp")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

`r paste(rxode2::rxode2(mod)$meta$population$disease_state)`. The cohort was
male BALB/c mice, 8-10 weeks old, 3-6 per timepoint with terminal sampling
(Singh 2015 Methods and Supplementary Material). RBC and HGB were measured only
on day 0 and day 10; all other markers were sampled over 0.25-96 h.

# Source trace

Every structural parameter and equation is traced to its location in Singh 2015
(main text Table 1 and Eqs. 1-22, the Supplementary Material derivation
Eqs. S1-S18, and the authors' ADAPT 5 control stream reproduced in the
Supporting Information). In-file `ini()` comments carry the same provenance.

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `ka`, `kel`, `kcp`, `kpc` | 8.5, 0.66, 0.014, 0.005 /h | Table 1 (Pharmacokinetics) |
| `vc` (apparent central volume) | 2.4 L at 30 mg/kg; 9.15 L at 10 mg/kg | Table 1 (V2/F, V1/F); dose-dependent |
| `kePHD2` (KE x PHD2tot0) | 9.9 /h | Table 1 (HIF1alpha); Eq. 3 / S17 |
| `IC50`, `g1` | 1.7 uM, 2.3 | Table 1; Eq. 1 / S15 |
| `kdeg_HIF` | 0 (fixed) | Table 1; Methods (PHD2-mediated degradation dominates) |
| `HIF1o` | 351 AU | Table 1; Eq. 4 (baseline) |
| `kdeg_mRNA`, `tau` | 0.43 /h, 2.7 h | Table 1; Eqs. 5-7, 11 |
| `EPO_mRNA0`, `EPO_plasma0` | 0.8, 0.047 ng/mL | Table 1; Eqs. 8-10 (baselines) |
| `g2` | 2.8 | Table 1; Eq. 5 |
| `Retic0`, `Tr`, `SL` | 4.6 %, 81 h, 0.2 | Table 1; Eqs. 14-16, 18 |
| `RBC0` | 10.76e12 cells/L (fixed) | Supplement S1 (observed baseline) |
| `MCH_average` | 16.04e-12 g/cell (fixed) | Table 1 (16e-12, fixed); ADAPT value |
| `Nkin` | 0.5226e10 cells/L/h | Supplement S1; ADAPT DIFFEQ code |
| HIF1alpha turnover | Eq. 3 / S17 | Methods / Supplement |
| EPO mRNA -> transit -> plasma | Eqs. 5-7 | Methods |
| Reticulocyte lifespan model | Eqs. 14-16 | Methods |
| Mature RBC, total RBC, HGB | ADAPT DIFFEQ XP(42); Eqs. 20, 22 | Supporting Information code / Methods |

```{r source-trace-ini}
knitr::kable(ui$iniDf[, c("name", "est")], caption = "Model parameters (ini).")
```

# Simulation setup

The two single-dose arms differ only in the oral dose amount and in the
dose-dependent apparent volume. PHI-1 amounts are the values coded in the
authors' ADAPT model (25.8 and 77.4 umol for 10 and 30 mg/kg), which give
plasma concentrations in uM when divided by the apparent volume. The 10 mg/kg
arm overrides `lvc` to `log(9.15)` (the model default is the 30 mg/kg value).

```{r simfun}
solve_arm <- function(amt, vc, tmax = 240, by = 0.25) {
  pars <- if (is.null(vc)) NULL else c(lvc = log(vc))
  ev <- et(amt = amt, cmt = "depot", time = 0) |>
    add.sampling(seq(0, tmax, by = by))
  s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, params = pars, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10,
               returnType = "data.frame")
  s
}

s30 <- solve_arm(amt = 77.4, vc = NULL) # default lvc = log(2.4), 30 mg/kg
s10 <- solve_arm(amt = 25.8, vc = 9.15) # 10 mg/kg
sim <- bind_rows(
  mutate(s30, dose = "30 mg/kg"),
  mutate(s10, dose = "10 mg/kg")
)
```

# Pharmacokinetics (Figure 2)

```{r fig2-pk, fig.cap = "Plasma PHI-1 after single oral doses of 10 and 30 mg/kg. Replicates Figure 2 of Singh 2015."}
ggplot(filter(sim, time <= 24), aes(time, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.7, linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = 20, y = 1.9, label = "IC50 = 1.7 uM", size = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma PHI-1 (uM)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Pharmacological responses (Figure 3)

```{r fig3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Kidney HIF1alpha, kidney EPO mRNA (relative), plasma EPO and reticulocytes. Replicates Figure 3 of Singh 2015."}
fig3 <- sim |>
  select(time, dose, hif1, epo_mrna, epo_plasma, retic) |>
  pivot_longer(c(hif1, epo_mrna, epo_plasma, retic),
    names_to = "marker", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(marker = factor(marker,
    levels = c("hif1", "epo_mrna", "epo_plasma", "retic"),
    labels = c(
      "Kidney HIF1a (AU)", "Relative EPO mRNA",
      "Plasma EPO (ng/mL)", "Reticulocytes (%)"
    )
  ))

xmax <- c("Kidney HIF1a (AU)" = 30, "Relative EPO mRNA" = 96,
          "Plasma EPO (ng/mL)" = 96, "Reticulocytes (%)" = 96)
fig3 <- fig3 |> filter(time <= xmax[as.character(marker)])

ggplot(fig3, aes(time, value, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Red blood cells, hemoglobin and PHD2 activity (Figure 4)

```{r fig4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "RBC, hemoglobin and the simulated active-PHD2 ratio. Replicates Figure 4 of Singh 2015."}
rbc_hgb <- sim |>
  select(time, dose, RBC, HGB, PHD2ratio) |>
  mutate(RBC = RBC / 1e12)

p_rbc <- ggplot(rbc_hgb, aes(time, RBC, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "RBC (1e12 cells/L)", colour = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(10, 12)) +
  theme_bw()
p_hgb <- ggplot(rbc_hgb, aes(time, HGB, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Hemoglobin (g/dL)", colour = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(16, 19)) +
  theme_bw()
p_phd2 <- ggplot(filter(rbc_hgb, time <= 24), aes(time, PHD2ratio, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "PHD2tot / PHD2tot0", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
print(p_rbc)
print(p_hgb)
print(p_phd2)
```

# NCA characterisation of plasma PHI-1

Singh 2015 reports the PK as rate constants (Table 1), not as NCA metrics. For
orientation we summarise the simulated 30 mg/kg plasma profile with PKNCA; the
grouping variable is the dose arm.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(dose, time, Cc)
# Defensive time-zero rows (one per arm) so AUC starts at t = 0.
conc <- bind_rows(
  conc,
  tibble(dose = unique(conc$dose), time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(dose, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(dose, time)

o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | dose)
d_intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                          auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, intervals = d_intervals))
nca <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  select(dose, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
knitr::kable(nca, digits = 3, caption = "NCA of simulated plasma PHI-1.")
```

# Validation checks

```{r checks}
# --- Baseline steady state (no dose): all markers constant ---------------
base <- solve_arm(amt = 0, vc = NULL, tmax = 240, by = 4)
rng <- function(x) max(x) / min(x) - 1
stopifnot(
  rng(base$hif1) < 1e-6,
  rng(base$retic) < 1e-6,
  rng(base$HGB) < 1e-6,
  abs(base$hif1[1] - 351) < 1e-6,
  abs(base$retic[1] - 4.6) < 1e-6
)

peak_fold <- function(s, col, base) max(s[[col]]) / base
# --- 30 mg/kg response magnitudes vs the Fig. 3 / Fig. 4 model curves -----
hif_fold <- peak_fold(s30, "hif1", 351) # Fig 3a solid ~ 23x
mrna_fold <- peak_fold(s30, "epo_mrna", 0.8) # Fig 3b solid ~ 2000x
epo_peak <- max(s30$epo_plasma) # Fig 3c solid ~ 45 ng/mL
retic_peak <- max(s30$retic) # Fig 3d solid plateau ~ 9 %
rbc_peak <- max(s30$RBC) / 1e12 # Fig 4a solid peak ~ 11.6
rbc_d10 <- s30$RBC[s30$time == 240] / 1e12 # Fig 4a solid at 240 h ~ 11.15
hgb_peak <- max(s30$HGB) # Fig 4b solid peak ~ 18.65
phd2_min <- min(s30$PHD2ratio) # Fig 4c solid ~ 0

stopifnot(
  hif_fold > 18 && hif_fold < 25,
  mrna_fold > 1800 && mrna_fold < 2600,
  epo_peak > 38 && epo_peak < 48,
  retic_peak > 8.6 && retic_peak < 9.6,
  rbc_peak > 11.5 && rbc_peak < 11.8,
  abs(rbc_d10 - 11.15) < 0.1,
  hgb_peak > 18.5 && hgb_peak < 18.9,
  phd2_min < 0.01
)

# --- 10 mg/kg is a minimal response (Fig. 3/4 dashed, near baseline) ------
stopifnot(
  max(s10$retic) < 4.8, # baseline 4.6; dashed line is flat
  max(s10$RBC) / 1e12 < 10.9, # baseline 10.76; essentially flat
  peak_fold(s10, "hif1", 351) < 3.5 # Fig 3a dashed ~ 2x
)

# --- Endogenous plasma EPO half-life = ln2 / (1/tau) = ln2*tau ------------
epo_thalf <- log(2) * 2.7
stopifnot(abs(epo_thalf - 1.87) < 0.05) # Discussion: "~1.8 hours" for mice

checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "HIF1a peak fold (30 mg/kg)", "EPO mRNA peak fold", "Plasma EPO peak (ng/mL)",
    "Reticulocyte plateau (%)", "RBC peak (1e12/L)", "RBC day 10 (1e12/L)",
    "HGB peak (g/dL)", "Active-PHD2 minimum", "Plasma EPO half-life (h)"
  ),
  Model = round(c(hif_fold, mrna_fold, epo_peak, retic_peak, rbc_peak,
                  rbc_d10, hgb_peak, phd2_min, epo_thalf), 3),
  `Paper (figure / text)` = c("~23x (Fig 3a)", "~2000x (Fig 3b)", "~45 (Fig 3c)",
    "~9 (Fig 3d)", "~11.6 (Fig 4a)", "~11.15 (Fig 4a)", "~18.65 (Fig 4b)",
    "~0 (Fig 4c)", "~1.8 (Discussion)")
)
knitr::kable(checks, caption = "Deterministic validation against Singh 2015 figures and text.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose-dependent apparent volume.** The paper describes the nonlinear PK with
  two apparent volumes, V1/F = 9.15 L at 10 mg/kg and V2/F = 2.4 L at 30 mg/kg
  (Table 1). The model carries a single `vc` whose default is the 30 mg/kg
  value; simulating the 10 mg/kg dose requires overriding `lvc` to
  `log(9.15)`, as done above. The absorption and disposition rate constants
  (`ka`, `kel`, `kcp`, `kpc`) are shared across doses.

* **PHI-1 dose amounts.** The oral amounts (25.8 and 77.4 umol for 10 and
  30 mg/kg) are the values coded in the authors' ADAPT model. They scale the
  two doses 3:1 and reproduce the fitted plasma concentrations when divided by
  the apparent volume; the mg/kg-to-umol conversion (mouse weight and molecular
  weight) is not stated for the undisclosed compound.

* **Mature-RBC production follows the authors' simulation code, not Eq. 19.**
  The published Eq. 19 writes mature-RBC production as the reticulocyte
  production delayed by the reticulocyte lifespan Tr, with loss at age
  Tr + TRBC. The authors' ADAPT simulation code that produced Figure 4
  (subroutine DIFFEQ, state `XP(42)`) instead drives mature-RBC production from
  the **current** plasma EPO with no Tr delay and no RBC-death term. The
  packaged model follows the code, so RBC and HGB reproduce Figure 4 (which the
  delayed form does not: it would postpone the RBC rise by ~81 h). The assumed
  24-day RBC lifespan therefore removes no cells within the published 10-day
  window and is not implemented; the reticulocyte lifespan model (Eqs. 14-16)
  is implemented exactly, including its Tr delay, and reproduces Figure 3d.

* **No residual error or IIV.** The fit was naive-pooled; the ADAPT control
  stream declares combined additive+proportional residual-error variance
  parameters for HIF1alpha, EPO mRNA, plasma EPO and reticulocytes, but Table 1
  reports no values for them. The model is therefore packaged as a
  typical-value simulation with no error model (as for the other QSP models in
  this library).

* **EPO mRNA data were means only.** The authors note the EPO mRNA endpoint had
  only mean (not individual pooled) data; the model fits the mean trajectory.

* **`kdeg_HIF` fixed to 0.** In the absence of drug, PHD2-mediated hydroxylation
  dominates HIF1alpha degradation, so the authors fixed the drug-independent
  degradation rate to 0 (Methods; Table 1).
```
